Macrons

Consonantal i

Body, health & movement

massage noun and verb

also massages, rub, rub down, rub-down, back rub

classical

M-O s.v. massage

fricō, fricāre, fricuī, frictum

verb, first conjugation

rub, rub down, massage

Passive fricārī: have a massage, be rubbed down.

Examples

  • numquam concessāmus lavārī aut fricārī aut tergērī aut ōrnārī

    we never stopped being bathed, rubbed down, dried and dressedPlaut. Poen. 219–220

  • hunc reficit in ipsō quoque itinere frequēns frictiō, post iter prīmum sedīle, deinde ūnctiō

    after a long walk, he is restored by frequent rubbing on the way, and after the walk first a seat, then an oilingCels. 1.3

  • Fricā mihi tergum, quaesō.

    Rub my back, please.composed

  • Vīsne ut tibi umerōs fricem?

    Shall I rub your shoulders?composed

  • Ah, quam bene est!

    Ah, that feels good!composed

Other words

  • frictiō, frictiōnis f. — a rub-down, massage

    noun, third declension · classical · Cels. 2.14

    Celsus gives it a chapter.

  • fricātiō, fricātiōnis f. — a rub-down, massage

    noun, third declension · also used · classical

  • malaxō, malaxāre — knead, soften, massage

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · M-O s.v. massage, citing Seneca, Ep. 66.53

    Scornful in Seneca, of pampered luxury.

See also masseur, rub with oil, relax, back.
